sections.description: Starred attributes keep their values, and a suggestion that matches on a value says so.
sections.changelog:
v1.4.0-dev.51 — Dev

  • A starred attribute keeps its value without being starred again. Every saved attribute was loaded with its value stripped: the limit the loader checks each value against was set further down the file than the line that loads them, so at that moment it was nothing at all, and every value failed the comparison and was dropped. Saving later worked, because by then the limit existed. That is why re-starring appeared to fix it and why it never lasted.
  • Attributes already sitting in the store with a blank value are not left behind. A starred name with no value of its own now borrows the values that name is actually used with on the site, so it is findable by its value straight away.
  • A suggestion that matched on its value now shows it as one. Typing ind lit those letters in the middle of a second word with nothing to say what that word was. The value is written onto the name as name="value" — which is also exactly what the suggestion inserts.

v1.4.0-dev.50 — Dev

  • The scrollbar no longer appears and disappears depending on which module you open. Settings was the one side panel that stopped the page scrolling behind it, so opening Settings hid the scrollbar and opening anything else brought it back. A full-width studio still holds the page still, because it covers it; a side panel does not, because there is no reason it should.
  • This was also why Settings kept measuring differently from its neighbours: with the scrollbar hidden the browser reports the window as 17px wider, which is the same 17px that was chased for three builds.
  • Scrolling inside a panel now stops at the panel instead of carrying on into the page behind it.

v1.4.0-dev.49 — Dev

  • The Workspaces icon stops moving. With nothing open it sat next to Settings; with a module open it sat next to the variable panel. Those are two different strips — the quick-access dial and the studio rail — and each decides its own order. Workspaces was in the right place in one and the wrong place in the other. It now sits immediately after the variable panel in both.
  • It had also been given the same ordering number as the variable panel, so where it landed on the rail was luck rather than intent. A check now refuses two tools sharing a number.

v1.4.0-dev.48 — Dev

  • The panel edges line up, and this time the cause is measured rather than guessed. Your own reading showed both panels at 468 wide but sitting 17px apart from the screen edge — the width of a scrollbar. The variable panel is placed by the stylesheet, which measures from the edge of the page; every studio was placed by script using a number that includes the scrollbar. On any page long enough to scroll, the two disagreed by exactly that much.
  • And the width is now one value instead of seven. MV already had a setting for how wide a side panel is, and only the variable panel was using it. Every studio reads it now, so they cannot drift apart again.

v1.4.0-dev.47 — Dev

  • The variable panel lines up with the studios. It sat 8px from the screen edge while every studio sat at 16, so it stuck out slightly further than the rest — which is what “slightly longer” was. Both docked sides are 16 now, and the heights already matched.

v1.4.0-dev.46 — Dev

  • The side modules really are one width now. dev.45 changed the width these panels are given, and nothing moved — Code Studio and CSS Studio are pinned by a stylesheet rule marked !important, which beats anything the panel is handed. Both pins, and the two places the code hard-coded the old number, are now 468.
  • Unchanged on purpose: the main variables panel is 370 and is not one of the side modules, and Content Studio, Media Studio, Plugin Studio, CSS Recipes and Documentation set their own widths.

v1.4.0-dev.45 — Dev

  • The side module panels are all one width. Code Studio, CSS Studio and Workspaces opened at 430px while Settings, Font Manager, Bricks Settings and Theme Styles opened at 468 — so switching between them shifted the edge. They are all 468 now, the widest of them, as asked.
  • Content Studio, Media Studio, Plugin Studio, CSS Recipes and Documentation are deliberately left alone: those are full studios whose docked layout is set by their own rules rather than by this width, and Documentation is meant to be wide.

v1.4.0-dev.44 — Dev

  • Removing a page from a workspace asks first. It deletes the workspace copy and anything you had edited in it, and it used to do that on one click with no warning. It now asks once, in place, and says plainly that your published page is not touched either way.
  • The CSS Recipes code editor no longer grows down the page. The editor measured the box it sits in and then resized itself to fill it — which made that box a few pixels taller, which started the measurement again. It now ignores its own echo, and the box is bounded by the form the way every other code editor already was.

v1.4.0-dev.43 — Dev

  • Workspaces opened onto a blur and nothing else in dev.42. Install this over it. The panel was reading seven things that were never declared, so it threw the moment it drew. A panel that throws still mounts and still dims the page — which is exactly what you saw.
  • The build had no way to notice. Reading a name nobody declared is not a syntax error, and every id was wired correctly, so both existing checks passed. There is now a third that runs each studio panel rather than reading it, and fails when a panel uses something declared nowhere. It was tested by putting the fault back and watching it fail.

v1.4.0-dev.42 — Dev

  • A workspace can hold a page. Add a Bricks page and MV makes a private copy of it. Open in Bricks opens the copy, so what you save goes to the copy and visitors keep seeing the published page. Remove it and the copy goes; the published page is never touched either way.
  • The copy is a WordPress draft, and that is the point. WordPress keeps drafts out of public queries by itself, so the privacy does not depend on MV running. Deactivate or delete MV and your visitors still see exactly what they saw before.
  • It still says what it does not do. Global classes, variables and theme styles are not held yet - editing those in a workspace still changes your live site, and the panel says so rather than implying it is protecting them. Private preview and publishing are the next two slices.
  • A page not built with Bricks is refused with a reason instead of copied into an empty shell, and the same page cannot be added twice.

v1.4.0-dev.41 — Dev

  • The WordPress plugin runtime remains unchanged from dev.40. This package retains the Workspaces rail correction and every earlier Dev fix while the development delivery record advances.

v1.4.0-dev.40 — Dev

  • dev.39 could make the studio rail disappear. Install this over it. Workspaces was added to seven of the eight lists that describe a studio and left out of the eighth — the one the rail reads to find which panel to sit beside. Opening Workspaces would have left the rail with no anchor and nothing on screen.
  • The Workspaces registration is now complete across the panel lifecycle, so opening that tool cannot blank the studio rail.

v1.4.0-dev.39 — Dev

  • Workspaces is on the studio rail. dev.38 shipped the engine with no way in — there was nothing to click. The rail now carries it first, before the studios that do the work, because “what am I working on” comes before the work.
  • The panel does what this slice can actually do, and says what it cannot. Name a workspace, rename it, archive it keeping everything, or discard it permanently behind a typed confirmation. It states plainly that nothing is captured yet — editing in Bricks, private preview and publishing are the next slices — rather than showing buttons that would imply otherwise.
  • A studio id is hand-kept in seven separate places, and missing one kills the button or the whole rail. A check now asserts every rail tool appears in all seven, so the next one cannot be half-registered.

v1.4.0-dev.38 — Dev

  • Workspaces begins. MV can now hold a named workspace — what you are about to change, and the moment its starting point was fixed. This first build is the record only: it does not read or write a single thing in Bricks, so it cannot alter what a visitor sees. Create, rename, archive and discard work; archiving keeps everything and discarding is a separate, permanent choice.
  • It refuses to overstate itself. A workspace reports that nothing is captured yet rather than implying it is protecting anything. Isolation gets claimed when it is built, per object family, and not before.
  • A table has been missing on fresh installs since v1.3.413. A line of prose sat inside the SQL that WordPress runs at activation, in a comment style MySQL does not have — so the statement after it failed and CSS Studio’s version history had no table to write to. Only new installs were affected; existing sites made the table before the comment was added.

v1.4.0-dev.37 — Dev

  • The module you open owns the fast lane. MV now sends at most one background request at a time and reserves another lane for your click, instead of making a 547ms response wait another 2.4 seconds behind speculative warm-up.
  • Clicking a module promotes its identical queued prefetch, and each response keeps its own timing data so concurrent calls cannot overwrite one another.

v1.4.0-dev.36 — Dev

  • Every MV response now says how long its own work took. WordPress boots in a third of a second, so the remaining wait is either MV answering or requests queueing behind each other - and those need completely different fixes. The report splits each slow call into MV, WordPress and queued.
  • Update checks and Media’s first page were each still being fetched more than once.

v1.4.0-dev.35 — Dev

  • The performance report was understating itself. It read zero cache hits while the store was doing all the work - the counters were on the layer underneath it. It now counts where a read is actually answered.
  • MV measures the server itself. One cheap call at idle splits a slow request into the part before MV runs - WordPress, every plugin, REST init - and MV own.

v1.4.0-dev.34 — Dev

  • Every read now shares one request, by construction. Routing modules through the shared store one at a time kept finding new ones - so the API client itself is the store now. Any component asking for a path shares one request and one freshness clock with every other, without knowing the store exists.
  • No caller busts the cache with a timestamp any more; the two that genuinely need this second’s value ask for it by name.

v1.4.0-dev.33 — Dev

  • The last two repeated requests are gone. Two components still read settings directly instead of through the shared store, and the CSS suggestions payload carried a cache-buster that made every call a different key - so it was fetched twice and neither copy could be reused.

v1.4.0-dev.32 — Dev

  • Media Studio no longer reads your whole media library to open. It fetched pages of 100 one after another - one of those pages took 21 seconds. The first page is 24 items and appears at once; the rest load behind the grid.
  • Diagnostics no longer runs when a module opens. It cost 20 seconds merely because a module became visible, and it has its own Rescan button.
  • Three separate update checks now share one.

v1.4.0-dev.31 — Dev

  • dev.30 did not load. Install this over it. The new runtime store was placed one level too deep - inside a closure rather than beside the code that calls it - so every module call was a ReferenceError and MV fell back to the reload button.
  • Nothing about the architecture changed; it is the same code at the right scope.
  • The boot check that missed it now compares where things live, not just that the file runs.

v1.4.0-dev.30 — Dev

  • Modules stop rebuilding themselves. Closing a panel used to unmount its whole subtree, so every effect and every request re-ran on the next open. Module data now lives outside the panel and survives it - a repeat open paints from memory and refreshes behind you.
  • Nothing blocks a panel opening. Stale data is shown while it is rechecked; a failed refresh never deletes data that still works.
  • The polls are gone. Figma pairing polled two endpoints every 2.5 seconds for as long as its panel existed. Update checks ran once per mount. Identical preference writes are no longer sent. Media Studio no longer runs a diagnostic scan just to open.
  • Cold start is warmed four ways - the page request, a session snapshot, one workspace bootstrap, and idle and hover prefetch.
  • veOpenReport() now counts cache hits, shared requests and skipped writes, and separates each open’s shell paint from its useful paint.

v1.4.0-dev.29 — Dev

  • A starred attribute is findable by its value again. A suggestion matched on its name and primary value only, and a pair saved with no value beside it normalises to a blank primary with the real value behind it - so it was built and filtered straight back out.
  • Code Studio closes the gap it makes. The Bricks left panel collapses its box rather than sliding over it, so the canvas takes the space instead of the page showing through.
  • The read cache is longer than one call. Four seconds could never hit on a server taking 5.6s a call, and a write now clears only what it touches.

v1.4.0-dev.28 — Dev

  • MV stops asking the same question twice. Your report showed 35 calls and 42 seconds of server time, with settings asked twice, update/check twice and user-preferences five times. An identical request already in flight is shared rather than sent again, and a read is remembered for four seconds so panels opening together pay once. Any write empties it.
  • Code Studio reshapes the builder around it. The Bricks left panel slides out and the Structure panel takes Code Studio’s width, both animated, both back on close.
  • Quick add’s suggestion trace records the saved records as the builder actually sees them.

v1.4.0-dev.27 — Dev

  • Every server call MV makes is timed. Run veOpenReport() in the builder console: it names the slowest calls, the ones made more than once, and what each studio open cost between the click and the first thing on screen.
  • A wait that is the server answering slowly, a wait that is many calls in a row, and a wait that is not the network at all look identical from the outside and are three different jobs.

v1.4.0-dev.26 — Dev

  • Quick add’s suggestions now say what they did. Every stage of the chain records what it produced and which one answered, on window.veLastSuggest - so a suggestion list that comes back empty can be read rather than guessed at.

v1.4.0-dev.25 — Dev

  • The page scrolls with Code Studio open. A full-viewport button was sitting over the page to catch a click-to-close - invisible, but it ate the wheel with it.
  • Closing on an outside click is a listener now rather than a layer. Clicking the canvas no longer closes Code Studio, which is the point of being able to work on the page while it is open; the X, Esc and Bricks’ own panels still close it.

v1.4.0-dev.24 — Dev

  • Alt+C now works after you click an element. The canvas is an iframe with its own document, and selecting an element puts the focus inside it - so the shortcut was being listened for in the one place the press could not arrive.
  • A live class rule stays on the page. The canvas kept it only for as long as Bricks felt like regenerating: leave the builder and come back and every editor still showed the rule while the page had lost it. MV paints its own copy for these rules too now.
  • The live-sync line is a line, not a card. A bordered panel with a button under it, for one sentence, was taking the room the code should have had.

v1.4.0-dev.23 — Dev

  • A code editor was eating Alt+C. The shortcut stepped aside whenever the caret was in a text field - and CodeMirror edits through a hidden textarea, so the press that opened Code Studio put the caret somewhere every later press was thrown away. A combo carrying Alt, Ctrl or Meta is not something a field means.
  • A live class edit now shows in Bricks’ own Custom CSS box. That box is a CodeMirror, and a CodeMirror shows its own document - Bricks fills it once when the control mounts. Every store write was reaching the canvas and Code2Bricks and leaving that box behind. MV types it in itself now, and only into an editor showing exactly what it is replacing.
  • A starred attribute can be found by typing its value, not only its name. The suggestion gate wanted a leading letter, so data-stagger="0.12" and data-anim-mobile-breakpoint="970" could not be reached by typing what they are.

v1.4.0-dev.22 — Dev

  • A live class edit now keeps reaching Bricks’ own box, not just the first keystroke. MV was putting a copy of the class record into the list it hands back; the canvas regenerates off the list, but Bricks’ class panel renders from the record it captured when you selected the class - so after the first write MV was updating a copy that panel never looks at. Its box froze on one keystroke while Code2Bricks caught up on its own.
  • Alt+C says what it did. A press that opens nothing and reports nothing cannot be told from one that never arrived - and with the panel shut there is nowhere to draw a message, which is exactly when it fails. It writes the decision to the console and to window.veLastEditClass.
  • The shortcut asked whether a different tool was disabled before opening Code Studio.

v1.4.0-dev.21 — Dev

  • The first Alt+C opened the class you edited last. The lane reads a stored request as it mounts, and nothing was writing one — the Bar dispatches the event itself and never went through the function that wrote it. So the first press came up on whatever was left over, and only the second landed right. The panel records the request from the event now, whoever sends it.
  • A live class edit now reaches Bricks’ own Custom CSS box. MV was building a fresh record for the class; the canvas regenerates off that, but Bricks’ class panel renders from the record it captured when you selected the class — an object a replacement never touches. Both are written now.
  • The sync report gained onCanvas, read from the canvas’ own stylesheet rather than from the copy MV just wrote — the half that can disagree.

v1.4.0-dev.20 — Dev

  • Alt+C did nothing and said nothing. It looked for the Bricks adapter only on the assembled window.MimamsBar - and the toast that should have explained lives on that same object, so it was skipped too. It reads the module’s own global first now.
  • The live sync records what it did - what was sent, whether the builder took it, and what the store holds half a second later.

v1.4.0-dev.19 — Dev

  • The Classes lane renders again. dev.17 and dev.18 drew it blank: the live Bricks sync read a value before it was declared, which throws on every render. Install this over either of them.

v1.4.0-dev.18 — Dev

  • Alt+C opens the selected element’s class, ready to edit. Where it used to take opening the studio, finding the class and pressing Edit.
  • It says Select an element with a class first rather than doing nothing, and Alt+C is a default rather than a decision.

v1.4.0-dev.17 — Dev

  • No Save button for a class rule that lives in Bricks. Typing writes straight into the copy the builder is holding, the way Bricks’ own Custom CSS box and Code2Bricks already mirror each other, and Bricks’ page save is what keeps it. Undo my changes puts back what was there.
  • Edits made in Bricks’ box or Code2Bricks come back the other way - never while the editor has focus.
  • A rule in a Code Studio stylesheet is MV’s own and keeps its Save.

v1.4.0-dev.16 — Dev

  • Saving a class rule asks before removing what it never opened. The same rule can be typed in two places at once, and MV was writing the copy it opened over the newer one without saying so. It names exactly what would go, and asks once.
  • Compared by meaning rather than spelling, so it does not fire on every save.

v1.4.0-dev.15 — Dev

  • The open rule editor comes back. The tab and the class were being restored and the editor was not. Whether it was open is stored against the class it was open on, and it reopens once.
  • The class-save report shows what the database holds, alongside the builder’s memory and what Code Studio is showing - three copies, where a report with only two can be read two opposite ways.

v1.4.0-dev.14 — Dev

  • A class edit reaches Bricks on save, not on the next reload. The database always had it; what did not hold was the copy in the open builder’s memory, which something replaces moments after MV writes it. MV writes it back, twice, a second apart.
  • Two attempts and not a loop - a page quietly fighting something for ever is worse than one that says it lost.

v1.4.0-dev.13 — Dev

  • Code Studio opens where you left it. The lane you were in, the sheet or class you had picked, and the place in the list you had scrolled to.
  • Everything remembered is checked before it is used: a sheet deleted since falls back, a tab name that is not one of the two falls back, and a corrupt store reads as empty. Nothing remembered can stop the panel opening.

v1.4.0-dev.12 — Dev

  • C37 narrowed. The report came back applied to the builder store and the rule still never reached Bricks - so the handoff is not failing. The store takes MV’s css and something puts the old copy back moments later.
  • The sync reads the store back twice, immediately and a second later, records what it is actually holding, and warns when that is no longer what MV wrote.

v1.4.0-dev.11 — Dev

  • A class rule saved in Code Studio could be quietly written back over. The open builder holds its own copy of every global class and writes it back when the page is saved. MV tells it about the new rule, but when that failed the panel still said Saved where it lives and the only trace was a console warning.
  • Being unable to tell the builder at all used to read as success. It does not now, and the panel says that saving the page would write the old copy back over the edit, and why.
  • mimamVarInspectClassSave('.your-class') reports what the last save actually did.

v1.4.0-dev.10 — Dev

  • A lifted suggestion list stays where it opened. It was pinned to position:fixed, but show-hint rewrites its position on every keystroke in page coordinates - so it walked down the screen and stopped flipping above the caret. It is absolute in page coordinates now.
  • A draft rule no longer needs !important. The preview stylesheet was in the head, and Bricks and Code2Bricks write theirs after it, so the saved rule won on source order. The draft goes at the end of the body now.
  • The theme card has an arrow back to the list and an x to close.

v1.4.0-dev.9 — Dev

  • A raised suggestion list keeps its skin. Moving the popup onto the body is what clears the tray, and it also took the popup out of the ancestors its styling is scoped to, so it arrived as a plain white box. Those ancestors now travel with it as class names on wrappers that draw nothing.
  • The theme card waits for an answer. It is shorter than the list it replaces, so the panel shrank out from under the pointer and the close timer took the card with it.
  • Its buttons are the product’s own buttons now, rather than a pair invented for the card.

v1.4.0-dev.8 — Dev

  • Clicking a theme in the rail list did nothing. The card asking whether the theme is for every MV editor or just this one was positioned absolutely inside a box sized by its content, so the moment it replaced the list the box collapsed and the card rendered at zero height. It is in flow now.
  • The suggestion lift reports whether it worked, not just what it tried: it names what is covering the list, its stacked z-index, and whether that thing is even in the same document.

v1.4.0-dev.7 — Dev

  • You no longer have to save to see what you are writing. Save is what commits a rule to the stylesheet the page reads, so the canvas used to show the last saved rule while you typed into a box that changed nothing. The rule you are editing is now painted into the builder as a stylesheet of its own.
  • It always comes off again - on Cancel, on Save, on closing the editor, on picking another class, and on the lane going away. A draft left behind would be worse than no preview at all.

v1.4.0-dev.6 — Dev

  • The theme list no longer disappears on the way to it. An empty gap between the rail button and the list meant a pointer crossing it was over neither, so the list closed and the click that followed landed on nothing. The gap is bridged and closing waits a moment.
  • It is centred on the rail and sits under the selected tool, with a dot so it reads as its own thing beside the tools rather than one of them.
  • A space in the Classes search no longer matches nothing. Class names have no spaces, so every space is stripped from the query: t h now finds what th finds.

v1.4.0-dev.5 — Dev

  • A theme control on the studio rail. Hover it and the nineteen themes open beside the rail, away from the panel so the code you are previewing stays visible. Hover any of them and the editors in that panel repaint live; leave and they go back to exactly what they were on. Nothing is saved by looking.
  • Choosing asks who it is for. The theme has always been one setting for the whole product, so only Everywhere in MV is written to it. Just this editor stays with that editor, and a later change in Settings leaves it alone.

v1.4.0-dev.4 — Dev

  • A saved attribute name remembers every value you star. The list was keyed by attribute name alone in the Bar, in Settings and on the server, and each of them overwrote the entry for a name it had already seen - so you ended up with as many rows as you had distinct names, however many values you starred.
  • A name holds up to 20 values, newest first. Settings lists one row per name and value, the star answers for the pair it sits on, and unstarring one value leaves the others.
  • Typing a bare name still suggests names, pre-filled with the value you starred most recently; the other values appear as you type toward them.

v1.4.0-dev.3 — Dev

  • Room between the rule editor and its buttons. Editing a class rule in Code Studio put Save and Cancel flush against the bottom of the code. The read-only rule box has always had 9px under it; the editor now has the same.
  • A suggestion list covered halfway down is now raised. The lift that keeps another plugin's autocomplete above Bricks' element tray only looked at the top few pixels of the list, so a tray crossing the middle of it went unnoticed. It samples the whole list now, and escalates above the highest thing covering it.

v1.4.0-dev.2 — Dev

  • Code Studio shows the page it is changing. It no longer blurs and dims everything behind it, so you can watch a rule take effect as you write it. Clicking off the panel still closes it.
  • Finding a class takes a few letters. The Classes search matches the letters in order rather than as a block — tbc reaches .telecom-benefits__container — and ranks the closest match first.

v1.4.0-dev.1 — Dev

  • Versions now describe the release, and suffixes count its test packages. Major, minor and patch regain their normal meaning; repeated builds on this feature line become 1.4.0-dev.2, not 1.4.1.
  • Release Manager orders Dev counters, Beta candidates and final releases correctly instead of discarding prerelease meaning.
  • Stable and Dev are the only active choices. An existing Beta account keeps a clearly labelled compatibility feed until Stable catches up, and is never silently moved to Dev or downgraded.

v1.3.606 — Dev

  • Code2Bricks’ suggestion list is no longer hidden behind the element tray. Their list uses CodeMirror’s stock stacking, which the tray sits well above, so half of what you were choosing from was painted underneath a toolbar.
  • MV raises that one list as it appears and nothing else — no stylesheet rule is shipped, so Bricks’ own editor, Advanced Themer’s and WPCodeBox’s are untouched.
  • It confirms the list is actually visible afterwards rather than assuming, and only moves it as a last resort.

v1.3.605 — Dev

  • A save writes what is in the box. Clicking Save blurred the code editor, and the editor’s text and the click landed in the same instant — so the save sent the rule as it stood before the edit.
  • The Code Studio code editor had the same fault and is fixed with it.
